gaps.sentence: There was plenty of food left, so the guests ___ have been hungry.
gaps.explanation: The evidence (leftover food) rules out hunger: can't have been.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better take an umbrella; it looks like rain.
We ___ have taken the wrong turning — the signpost was knocked down in the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'May have + participle' offers one possible explanation of a past event.

gaps.sentence: We ___ hurry — the doors close in five minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' expresses urgent advice: had better hurry.

gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
You ___ better not be late again; the boss is getting tired of it.
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'had better' places 'not' after 'better': had better not be.

gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.
